issues.description: The UML diagram in the problem statement names the class 'Course' while the exercise text and repository refer to the class as 'Lecture'. This inner-artifact name mismatch may confuse students about the intended class name and where to follow the UML for attribute order and constructor parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML diagram in the problem statement to use the class name 'Lecture' (instead of 'Course') so it matches the textual description, template, and solution. Ensure any references to the UML (e.g., constructor parameter order) clearly refer to the 'Lecture' class.

issues.description: The problem text and template expect a Lecture class (and the exercise repeatedly refers to 'Lecture' and attributes like lectureName), but the UML diagram in the problem statement declares the class as Course. This mismatch (Lecture vs. Course) can confuse students mapping the UML to the provided template and solution, as they may look for or expect a Course class instead of the Lecture class present in the template and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML diagram in the problem statement to use the class name 'Lecture' (and corresponding attribute names) instead of 'Course' so the UML, the textual description, the template, and the solution consistently refer to the same class name.
